states: Embedded production build of this change, served by a private DEMO_MODE mock backend (50 Proxmox nodes, 929 guests, PULSE_TELEMETRY=false); an embedded build of the unchanged base ran beside it for comparison. The build base differs from bd4f6e36c4 only by two unused helpers in utils/format.ts and utils/status.ts, which tree-shaking drops

Proxmox overview in Trends mode at 1440x900: 12 of 12 visible node rows draw CPU, memory and disk sparklines (36 with data) and 140 of 140 rendered guest rows draw history sparklines (420 with data), identical to the base build
Proxmox overview in Trends mode at 390x844: 6 of 6 node rows (18 sparklines) and 36 of 36 guest rows (108 sparklines) draw history, identical to the base build
Network: one /api/charts/workloads and one /api/charts/infrastructure read on load and one of each on the next 30-second poll, matching the base build

Storage: no pulse.infrastructureSummaryCharts.* or pulse.workloadsSummaryCharts.* localStorage keys, no Storage.setItem/removeItem calls on those prefixes and no JSON.stringify output over 200k characters during 75 seconds; the base build serialized 924,249 and 9,629,902 characters per poll (5-31 ms each) and then removed both keys because they exceeded the 900k cap
interactions: Demo sign-in, then load /proxmox with the Workloads display mode stored as Trends (sparklines)
Hold the page through a 30-second history poll and re-count sparklines, chart requests and localStorage keys
Wrap Storage.setItem/removeItem and JSON.stringify before load to record summary-cache storage traffic and large serializations on both builds
